source.title: How Do Large Language Models Acquire Factual Knowledge During Pretraining?
source.authors: Hoyeon Chang; Jinho Park; Seonghyeon Ye; Sohee Yang; Youngkyung Seo; Du-Seong Chang; Minjoon Seo

record.file_problem: The full text is present. No apparent truncation or garbling affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how batch size, model size, and training conditions affect acquisition and retention of fictional factual knowledge. Those results extend work on generalization dynamics to LLM pretraining, but do not measure the same-distribution natural-label test error or gap in any listed version.
record.gate_note: The study uses fictional facts deliberately absent from pretraining and evaluates their memorization, paraphrased semantic generalization, and compositional generalization. These are distinct from same-distribution natural-label test error. Results about batch size and model size are recorded as findings that fit no version; no listed version is directly tested.
record.test_reason: The study measures acquisition and forgetting of injected fictional facts through cloze-target log probabilities. None of V1–V8 is tested. In particular, the batch-size experiment measures normalized retention after controlled injections, not held-out performance under equal epoch or token budgets, so it does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' main interpretation: factual knowledge accumulates through incremental log-probability gains followed by forgetting, with reported power-law forgetting and greater retention under paraphrased-data and larger-batch recipes. It omits their finding that immediate acquisition improves with model size but not significantly with pretraining progress. Deduplication benefits, long-tail learnability, and consequences for generated answers are interpretations or hypotheses rather than directly measured generation outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: Continued OLMo pretraining with injected fictional facts; measures log-probability acquisition and retainability rather than same-distribution training and test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, injection scenario (duplication versus paraphrase), acquisition depth, model size, and pretraining stage affect measured acquisition or forgetting dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: At the 7B Mid checkpoint, batch-128 decay constants exceed batch-2048 constants for all six injection-by-depth conditions: duplication 0.31/0.29/0.26 versus 0.25/0.25/0.20; paraphrase 0.31/0.32/0.26 versus 0.21/0.23/0.15. The reduced-batch experiment also reinitializes optimizer state.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these continued-pretraining recipes, batch-128 runs forget a larger fraction of acquired factual log-probability gains than batch-2048 runs; this does not establish a fixed-budget generalization effect or isolate batch size alone.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch 2048 and the Mid checkpoint, paraphrase injection has lower decay constants than duplication at every acquisition depth: 0.21 versus 0.25, 0.23 versus 0.25, and 0.15 versus 0.20. The record's statement that these selected values are nonuniform is incorrect. Broader results do contain exceptions, including Late-checkpoint composition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Paraphrase injection is associated with slower normalized forgetting than duplicate injection in the selected Mid-checkpoint conditions; the pattern depends on checkpoint and acquisition depth.

record.problems: The study does not evaluate model generation output or establish the relation between accumulated probability and generated answers. It tests one reduced batch size (128 versus 2048), uses fictional injected knowledge, and does not study batch-size and learning-rate effects across multiple values. The OLMo-1B Early checkpoint has unstable dynamics and its decay fits are omitted or poor in reported analyses.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows omitted. Other model sizes, stages, injection counts, and decay estimates are reported in figures or tables but are outside the strongest batch-size comparison extracted here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including training-set size, underfitting, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, training-test gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All twelve numerical values match the supplied tables. Retainability is normalized relative to pre-injection log probability and the final local acquisition maximum. No verdict-bearing results are missing for V1–V8. Controlled knowledge injection alone is not the exclusion reason; the measured constructs and experimental comparisons do not match the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label test accuracy and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under tuning.
Held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and the listed batch-size recipe adjustments.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to training-test error gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relation.reason: The study discusses memorization and generalization, but its own experiments address factual acquisition and retention rather than any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study measures acquisition and forgetting of injected factual knowledge through cloze-target log probabilities; it neither tests nor uses V1–V8. Its batch-size comparison does not measure V5's held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.

source_check.notes: Appendix G's reduced-batch runs reinitialize optimizer state and use each checkpoint's initial learning rate (0.000237 for OLMo-7B Mid, Table 5); comparison with Table 2 does not isolate batch size. All listed values match the tables, and normalized factual retention cannot determine V1–V8.
